correctness.rationale: After affine normalization, the Euclidean point-reflection maximum is the Rogers--Shephard value \(2^n/n!\) at a simplex vertex. The relative ball volume follows from simplex equality in the difference-body theorem. Its polar is the coordinate-range polytope and has volume \((n+1)2^n\) by an exact sign-chamber integral. The Gromov-mass cross-polytope determinant reduces to complete-graph incidence minors, hence total unimodularity gives the exact maximum. The mass* case polarizes to a cross-polytope whose determinant maximum is exactly \(2^nD_n\). The bundled checker independently reconstructs the relevant polytopes and determinants in dimensions \(2,3,4\); the universal proof uses the stated exact structural lemmas rather than finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Simplices are the canonical equality cases for both classical Rogers--Shephard inequalities and therefore the natural benchmark family for the open relative-norm extension. The result determines all four standard volumes simultaneously in every dimension and exposes a structural link between mass* and the classical zero-one maximal determinant. This is a family-level exact reduction rather than a routine low-dimensional calculation.
